checks: The Schengen short-stay visa framework covers stays of up to 90 days in any 180 days. Airport transit visas are a distinct requirement.
Schengen mainland/core jurisdictions; third-country short-stay travelers
Check nationality, purpose, residence and transit exemptions separately. Cyprus and Ireland have separate visa rules.
The Entry/Exit System is fully operational at external borders and electronically records entry and exit for covered short-stay travelers.
External Schengen crossings; covered third-country nationals
Check personal exemptions and border procedure. ETIAS has a separate launch and application process.
Travelers entering or leaving EU territory with EUR 10,000 or more in covered cash or equivalent must declare it.
EU external border cash controls; core jurisdictions
European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union
Check intra-EU national controls, unaccompanied cash, and territorial scope separately.
Personal alcohol and tobacco allowances apply on arrival from outside the EU excise area, with lower tobacco allowances possible and age limits.
EU VAT and excise core areas; personal luggage
National allowances and product-specific bans require separate checks. Overseas and special fiscal territories excluded from expansion.
EU rules require a phytosanitary certificate for covered plants and plant products in passenger luggage. Pineapple, coconut, durian, banana and date fruits are listed exemptions.
Entry into the EU plant health area from outside it; core jurisdictions
Check protected-zone and commodity restrictions. Covered plant rules do not resolve meat, dairy or other animal product rules.

Meat and dairy generally cannot enter from outside the covered European area in personal luggage. Listed exceptions apply, including specified quantities of some infant or medical foods and separate origin rules for Greenland and Faroe Islands.
Personal luggage at EU entry; origin- and product-dependent
Check origin, quantities, temporary disease controls and protected zones.
Non-commercial entry of a dog, cat or ferret from most non-EU origins requires health documentation and entry checks. The Commission provides the current certificate model and separate exemptions.
EU entry with a dog, cat or ferret; core jurisdictions
Check country lists, rabies timing/titer, designated entry points, quantity and owner travel exceptions, and destination-specific tapeworm rules.
A valid full EU-issued driving licence is generally recognized in other EU countries. Travelers with a non-EU licence should check the destination authority.
EU core jurisdictions; recognition of driving documents
Check local age restrictions, category, non-EU licence and permit rules. Local road rules need a separate review.

Where operator registration is required, a visitor residing outside the EASA area registers through the authority in the first EASA state of intended operation. Member states set local geographic operating zones.
EASA states listed by the agency; core jurisdictions only
Check aircraft class, mass, sensors, training, airspace maps and local permissions. Customs entry of the equipment is separate.
Great Britain applies personal food-product restrictions that vary by product and origin. Northern Ireland has separate guidance.
England, Scotland and Wales; personal food imports
Check the origin and product pages for live disease restrictions and exemptions.
Cash of GBP 10,000 or more must be declared for covered movements between Great Britain and countries outside the UK.
Great Britain international movements; Northern Ireland and route-specific rules are distinct
Check group totals, covered instruments and special routes.
Visitors must declare food, plants and animal products at arrival. Admissibility depends on the item and origin.
Check product, origin and current Canadian Food Inspection Agency restrictions.
Travelers entering or leaving Canada must report cash or monetary instruments totaling CAD 10,000 or more.
Canadian ports of entry and exit
Check reporting procedure and covered instruments for the route.
The arrival declaration covers biosecurity risk goods, including foods, plant and animal products and outdoor gear that can carry soil or pests.
New Zealand border and MPI screening
Declare and verify item-specific admissibility. No extension to Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau.
Travelers carrying NZD 10,000 or more in cash or its foreign equivalent into or out of New Zealand must complete a Border Cash Report.
Check covered instruments and filing instructions before travel.
Plants and animals subject to quarantine must be presented at the appropriate inspection counter before customs examination.
Japan passenger baggage; plant and animal quarantine
Check product, origin and inspection or certification exceptions with the competent quarantine authority.
Japan Customs identifies CITES restrictions for protected plants and animals and some products derived from them.
Japan passenger imports; protected specimens and derivatives
Check species and required documents with Japan's CITES authority. Export controls need separate review.
Controlled goods require any applicable permit or authorization before arrival and must be presented with supporting documents at the Red Channel or Customs Examination Area.
Check the prohibited and controlled lists and relevant licensing authority. This is a procedural finding.
Singapore lists chewing gum as prohibited from import with an exception for Health Sciences Authority-approved oral dental and medicinal gum.
Singapore import controls for chewing gum
Check whether a particular gum qualifies and whether separate requirements apply.
